protectedRevelations: FIRE model and culminating philosophical wager

scenes.title: Purpose can mislead
scenes.viewerPurpose: Question whether a strong purpose must be good Ask what a meaningful life must answer for
scenes.composition: A forceful purpose statement sits beside its effect on another person
addOrChange: Remove roof-leak distraction and evil-symbol shorthand.

cues.narration: A life can feel full of purpose while serving something terrible.
cues.visualAction: Show confident purpose while the affected person hesitates.

cues.narration: The Ultimate Sense of Life begins by asking what meaning must answer for.
cues.visualAction: Bring both people into the book’s question about meaning.

scenes.title: Many ways of meaning
scenes.viewerPurpose: Expect ideas grounded in an individual human life See no single voice claiming the whole answer
scenes.composition: Several traditions surround one ordinary personal question
addOrChange: Replace comic support telephone with three distinct books, without caricatures.

cues.narration: It brings psychology, religion, and philosophy into a question we usually face one life at a time.
cues.visualAction: Open psychology, religion and philosophy beside the same note.

cues.narration: None gets to speak for the whole human experience.
cues.visualAction: Keep their answers separate instead of merging them into certainty.

scenes.title: The ordinary witness
scenes.viewerPurpose: Meet humor and ordinary people among the big arguments Feel a meal matter without a theory of everything
scenes.composition: A shared meal follows a small useful repair
addOrChange: Replace storm and roof sequence with a repaired table and ordinary food.

cues.narration: Comic conversations and ordinary witnesses bring grand arguments back to work, care, grief, and affection.
cues.visualAction: The people share a quiet amused moment after finishing the repair.

cues.narration: A well-made meal can matter before anyone explains the universe.
cues.visualAction: Serve the meal without a cosmic explanation appearing above it.

scenes.title: What deserves your life
scenes.viewerPurpose: Find room for doubt and humor while thinking seriously Ask which purpose you would want to live for
scenes.composition: The open book remains on the same lived-in table
addOrChange: Remove payment and excluded-person subplot, retaining a margin question.

cues.narration: There is room here for readers who want to think deeply and still keep their doubts and humor.
cues.visualAction: A reader smiles at a passage before pausing over the question.

cues.narration: What makes a purpose worth living for, even when life gives us no final explanation?
cues.visualAction: Hold ordinary life around the unanswered question.
